SCOPe 2.08 places the bulge domain in superfamily b.84.5 'V1 ATP synthase A subunit, bulge domain-like' (sunid 310577), one of five superfamilies under fold b.84 'Barrel-sandwich hybrid' (sunid 51229; fold comment: 'sandwich of half-barrel shaped beta-sheets') in class b (all-beta). The sibling superfamilies are b.84.1 Single hybrid motif (biotinyl/lipoyl carrier domains; '7 to 8 strands in 2 beta-sheets'), b.84.2 Rudiment single hybrid motif (e.g. cytochrome f small domain), b.84.3 Duplicated hybrid motif ('half-barrel sheet of 8 strands sandwiched with two 3-stranded sheets', e.g. LytM), and b.84.4 Ribosomal L27 protein-like ('rudiment single hybrid fold with a permuted topology'). b.84.5 contains a single family b.84.5.1 with two protein entries: 'V1 ATP synthase A subunit, bulge domain' (Thermus thermophilus HB8 and Saccharomyces cerevisiae) and 'A1 ATP synthase A subunit, bulge domain' (Pyrococcus horikoshii). Representative domains are d3a5ca3 (3a5c A:113-184, T. thermophilus A3B3 complex with ADP) and d3ikja2 (3ikj A:114-190, P. horikoshii). The superfamily is annotated with PubMed 19893485 (the T. thermophilus A3B3 crystal structure paper). The sunids in the 310000 range indicate this is a SCOPe-era addition rather than a node inherited from SCOP 1.75.

Why a separate superfamily rather than a family inside b.84.1-b.84.4: in SCOP/SCOPe, the fold level records only that domains have the same major secondary structures in the same arrangement and topology, which can arise by convergence or physical constraints; the superfamily level is the lowest level at which curators assert probable common evolutionary origin, usually on the basis of sequence, structural and functional features beyond the shared core. The bulge is a roughly 70-residue insertion within the P-loop nucleotide-binding domain of the catalytic A subunit of V/A-type ATPases (absent from F1 beta subunits), with no detectable sequence similarity to biotinyl/lipoyl swinging-arm carriers, cytochrome f, peptidoglycan hydrolase LytM, or ribosomal L27, no shared functional site (it does not carry a lipoyl/biotinyl lysine and is not a prosthetic-group carrier), and a completely different genomic and structural context (an intradomain insertion in a rotary ATPase). Its beta-sandwich of half-barrel sheets matches the b.84 fold, so SCOPe records that architectural similarity at the fold level, but curators found nothing beyond the fold to justify asserting common ancestry, so they gave it its own superfamily. The deterministic comparison of d3a5ca3 (b.84.5.1) with cytochrome f small domain d1vf5c2 (b.84.2.2) confirms the lowest shared node is fold b.84 ('same_fold'; interpretation: structural similarity, not by itself homology), with no caveats, heterogeneity or warnings on either domain.
